summary.text: 就 is now commonly used for ‘go to’ or ‘approach,’ among other senses. Its early graphic history is disputed: one reported analysis sees a temple above a high platform, while accounts disagree about the lower element and the early graphs’ relation to the later verb.

formation.text: A secure single formation analysis is not established. Early graphs are reported as 亯 over 京, interpreted as a temple above a raised platform and proposed to depict ritual at height; the ritual interpretation and identification of those graphs with the later verb remain uncertain. The Qin and small-seal form is reported as 京 + 尤, matching the Eastern Han dictionary’s analysis, but another paleographic account proposes that some early lower elements were 止 and that later 又/尤 forms arose through graphic confusion. Thus the later graph can be described as a proposed semantic compound, but 尤’s role as a phonetic element is not established by the cited sound evidence.

components.text: In the reported early form, 亯 is interpreted as a temple, contributing the depicted setting in the proposed ritual-at-height scene. The graph reports support this component analysis, but the early examples are mostly place names and their identification with the later verb is unsettled.

京 is analyzed as a tall platform or tower and contributes the raised setting in the proposed early scene. It is also named alongside 尤 in the Eastern Han dictionary’s account of the later graph; this does not show that the earliest graph had 尤.

尤 appears in the reported Qin and small-seal form and in the Eastern Han dictionary’s analysis. Another account proposes 止 as an earlier lower element, with later 又/尤 forms resulting from graphic confusion; 尤’s historical role in 就 remains disputed.

sound_limitation.text: Current Mandarin readings form a usable comparison, but the cited Old Chinese reconstructions do not closely match, and this comparison does not establish 尤 as the historical phonetic component.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings share an initial glide and rhyme but differ in tone and initial: 尤 yóu, 就 jiù. The cited Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions, *[ɢ]ʷə and *[dz]u[k]-s, do not provide a close direct match.

history.text: Reported oracle-bone and bronze forms contain 亯 above 京; Chu forms are said to share strokes between them. Qin slips show 京 + 尤, the form reported as informing small-seal 就. These are source-reported analyses; no glyph image was visually inspected here.

A competing paleographic analysis proposes an early lower 止 and suggests that later 又/尤 forms reflect graphic confusion. The Eastern Han dictionary records the analysis 从京从尤 and a Zhou-script form 𡰜, but this later testimony alone does not settle the earliest graph.

uncertainties.text: The available accounts do not settle whether the mostly place-name oracle-bone examples represent the later verb 就, what their lower element was, or whether the proposed ritual-at-height scene is the character’s original meaning. The dossier supplies no settled graphic sequence linking all reported forms.

Although the later form includes 尤 in some accounts, its phonetic role is not secured: the cited Old Chinese reconstructions do not offer a close match, and the early lower element itself is disputed.

senses.period: oracle-bone inscriptions; exact dating and identification unresolved
senses.text: The earliest reported examples are mostly place names. Their identification with the later verbal character is not settled, so this is an attested use of the early graph, not a secure original meaning of the word 就.
The phrase 申就乃命 is reported as a verbal use with a sense near ‘complete.’ Its relation to the proposed early place-name use or ritual-at-height interpretation is not established.
A Warring States route list is reported with 就 meaning ‘go to.’ The evidence does not establish a continuous semantic development from ‘high’ or ‘complete’ to this use.
‘Approach’ and ‘near’ are supplied as current glosses. The dossier does not document when these senses arose or establish their path from earlier uses.
‘Just’ and ‘simply’ are supplied as current glosses. The dossier does not establish their chronology or semantic connection to the historical attestations.

limitations.text: The proposed ritual-at-height interpretation, early place-name examples, and later verbal uses are not connected by a demonstrated semantic chronology; they are kept as separate attestations.
Current glosses do not establish when meanings arose or how they developed from earlier uses.

overview.text: 就 is commonly used for ‘go to’ and ‘approach.’ Its early form is interpreted as a temple above a raised platform, but scholars disagree about the lower part and how the earliest graphs relate to the later verb.

components.text: 亯 is interpreted as a temple, the setting in one proposed reading of the early graph.
京 is read as a raised platform or tower, supplying the high setting in that proposed scene.
尤 occurs in the reported later form, but another analysis proposes an earlier 止; 尤’s role and the graphic change remain disputed.

relationships.text: In the proposed early 亯 + 京 analysis, 亯 depicts a temple as part of a ritual-at-height scene; the reading of the graph’s early uses and this interpretation remain unsettled.

京 depicts the raised platform or tower in the proposed early scene. The accounts also report 京 in the later form and in the Eastern Han dictionary’s analysis; this edge describes the depicted role in the proposed early scene.

尤 is present in the reported Qin and small-seal form and is interpreted in the Eastern Han dictionary as contributing the idea ‘different from the ordinary.’ Its role in the earliest graph is disputed, and the cited sound comparison does not establish it as phonetic.
